title: "Angles and Orthogonality"

**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.4. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

Angle measures relative direction independently of vector length. In regression, a residual vector perpendicular to the model's column space signals an optimum of ordinary least squares.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\cos\theta=\frac{\boldsymbol x^\top\boldsymbol z}{\|\boldsymbol x\|_2\|\boldsymbol z\|_2}
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

For x=(1,0) and z=(0,2), the dot product is zero, so the angle is 90 degrees. For x=(1,1) and z=(2,2), cosine similarity is one, despite the different lengths.

## What follows, and what does not

The formula requires nonzero vectors. Orthogonality is defined relative to the chosen inner product, and it generalises beyond familiar three-dimensional arrows.

## Test your reasoning

Can two vectors with cosine similarity -1 be considered parallel? In which orientation?
